summary.headline: Kalpataru Q2 FY27 pre-sales fell 5% to INR 1,258 crore, but FY27 pre-sales guidance of INR 6,500 crore was held unchanged.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 pre-sales were INR 1,258 crore, down 5% YoY, with H1 flat at INR 2,587 crore. Sales collections were flat at INR 1,189 crore in Q2 and up 9% YoY at INR 2,554 crore in H1. Revenue under the project completion method was INR 437 crore in Q2 and INR 909 crore in H1, with a reported loss of INR 71 crore in Q2 and INR 100 crore in H1. Management said H2 should be better than H1, with about 60% of the INR 6,500 crore guidance still to come and three launches planned for Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: Kalpataru Park City, Thane
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 pre-sales of about INR 420 crore vs INR 167 crore in H1 FY26, up about 130%. Walk-ins up 25% YoY and conversion nearly doubled; over 2,000 families now resident on site.

segments.name: Kalpataru Elaara, Bangur Nagar, Goregaon West
segments.commentary: Launched mid-September 2026 with 2, 3 and 4 BHK residences; 30% sold at time of call.

segments.name: Kalpataru Vian, Lokhandwala
segments.commentary: Launched in Q1 FY27; sales momentum continued into Q2.

segments.name: Kalpataru One, Worli
segments.commentary: Management reports strong customer interest and conversion improving in the festive season; no volume figure given.

segments.name: Plotted development (Nagpur and Karjat)
segments.commentary: Plotted projects in Nagpur and Karjat; no sales or revenue figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales guidance unchanged at INR 6,500 crore; about 40% achieved in H1, with roughly 60% expected in H2 based on historical pattern.
Net debt at FY27 year-end expected to be flat versus FY26 levels.
Net operating and gross cash flows expected to be broadly in line with FY26, scaled to higher pre-sales (FY26 pre-sales INR 5,280 crore).
Target of 5.5 million sq ft completions in FY27; about 2.3 million sq ft already completed in H1.
About 14 million sq ft of ongoing projects to complete across FY27-FY29; the remainder after FY27 falls in FY28 and FY29.
Management expects H2 FY27 to be better than H1, with some projects completing and recognising first-time revenue and profit in H2.
risks_watch: Q2 pre-sales down 5% YoY; H2 must deliver about 60% of INR 6,500 crore guidance, relying on festive sustenance sales and three launches.
Launch timelines for Suman Nagar, Ardene (Nagpur) and Blossoms (Pune) depend on pending IOD, final approval and RERA steps.
Net debt-to-equity at 2.1x and net debt of INR 8,323 crore; management guides net debt flat, so deleveraging depends on H2 completions and collections.
Revenue recognition under project completion method makes quarterly revenue and profit lumpy; H1 loss of INR 100 crore with first-time H2 recognition expected.
Kalpataru One (Worli) conversion improvement is described qualitatively only; no sales figures disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and execution, with specific targets reiterated. Cautious on near-term sales: Q2 pre-sales were down and management relies on H2 launches and festive sales. Several answers were brief or unquantified, for example on Kalpataru One and the cash flow outlook.
key_quotes: Our guidance for pre-sales for FY27 remains unchanged at INR 6,500 crore.
It has been a usual trend that, and we have met that trend, that 40% of the pre-sales guidance is generally met in the H1, and around 60% is met in H2.
The demand seems healthy across everywhere, and I'll break it down.
The price rise has happened up to 3% -5% in the projects, and it has taken care of the increase in inflation and cost of product now and what we anticipate in the future.

qa_highlights.question: Sourabh Gilda (JM Financial) asked for a bridge between H1 pre-sales of close to INR 2,600 crore and the FY27 guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 40% of the INR 6,500 crore guidance is achieved in H1; H2 will rely mainly on sustenance sales from ongoing projects and a few launches (Suman Nagar Chembur, Blossoms Pune, Ardene Nagpur), with the October to March festive period key. Management said H1 at 40% and H2 at about 60% is the usual pattern they have met.

qa_highlights.question: Sourabh Gilda asked for the status and timing of the three launches (approvals and whether they are back-ended or during festive season).
qa_highlights.answer: Suman Nagar (Chembur): IOD received and resident vacation under way, launch expected in Q4 FY27. Nagpur plotted project: pre-approval received, final approval expected in about one and a half months, then RERA, launch in Q4. Blossoms (Pune): RERA applied, launch expected before December.

qa_highlights.question: Sourabh Gilda asked whether any price segment is showing demand slowdown or moderation across the portfolio from INR 2 crore to luxury Worli.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is healthy across segments: good response under INR 3 crore (Thane, Mira Road, Pune, Western suburbs, plots), INR 3 to 10 crore in Western Mumbai launches and under-construction projects, and good walk-in interest in the SoBo luxury market.

qa_highlights.question: Vishal Singh (individual investor) asked for the year-end net debt guidance, whether year-end pre-sales guidance is achievable, plotted development details and cash flow outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt at FY27 year-end to be flat versus FY26 levels, with capital consumed by execution and some business development spend. Plotted development is in Nagpur and Karjat. Pre-sales guidance is INR 6,500 crore. Net operating and gross cash flows expected to be broadly the same as FY26, which had pre-sales of INR 5,280 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Ashi (MyCel Advisors) asked which projects await approvals that could delay launches, and how much price-hike headroom remains for future phases.
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated three launches (Chembur, Pune, Nagpur plotting), all on track for Q3 and Q4. Price increases of 3% to 5% taken across projects, which management said covers current inflation and cost increases and anticipated future costs; no further headroom quantified.

capex_capacity: Target of 5.5 million sq ft of completions in FY27; about 2.3-2.37 million sq ft already completed in H1 FY27 (over 2,200 units delivered in H1).
Q2 FY27 occupation certificates received for 1.58 million sq ft across ~1,500 units.
About 14 million sq ft of ongoing projects to complete across FY27, FY28 and FY29 gradually; about 5.5 million sq ft of this in FY27, remainder in FY28 and FY29.
Kalpataru Park City, Thane: over 2,000 families resident on site; management expects over 3,000 families by end of next year (FY28), with key retail outlets turning operational.
Projects completing in H2 FY27 are expected to yield first-time revenue and profit recognition under the project completion method.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as healthy across price bands: under INR 3 crore demand seen in Thane, Mira Road, Pune and Western suburbs, plotted projects also selling well.
INR 3 crore to INR 10 crore bracket: Western Mumbai launches at Lokhandwala (Vian) and Bangur Nagar (Elaara) saw good response, and under-construction projects are selling well.
Luxury segment in SoBo: good walk-in and interest; management said conversions will follow in the next few months.
Kalpataru One, Worli: strong customer interest; conversion began improving in the festive season, no volume figure given.
Pricing: price increases of 3% to 5% taken across projects, management said this covers current and anticipated inflation and cost increases.

Pre-sales guidance FY27 unchanged at INR 6,500 crore; about 40% achieved in H1 and management expects about 60% in H2 driven by sustenance sales through the October-March festive period plus launches.

adds.what: 5.5 million sq ft of completions targeted in FY27 (about 2.3 million sq ft done in H1); not new productive capacity, project completions

growth.why: FY27 pre-sales guidance held at INR 6,500 crore (about 40% achieved in H1, ~60% expected in H2 from festive sustenance sales and three launches), and 5.5 million sq ft completion target held with 2.3 million sq ft done in H1; Q2 pre-sales fell 5% YoY, so the guidance is only partly backed by specific launches and completions.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 adjusted EBITDA margin was 18.4% and Q2 was 16.6%; first-time revenue and profit recognition from projects completing in H2 and 3% to 5% price increases should help, but no margin guidance was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Target of 5.5 million sq ft completions in FY27 with about 2.3 million sq ft done in H1 and about 14 million sq ft of ongoing projects to complete across FY27-FY29; these are project completions, not new productive capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 pre-sales of INR 2,587 crore are about 40% of the INR 6,500 crore guidance, with about 60% expected in H2 from festive sustenance sales and three launches; Q2 pre-sales were down 5% YoY, so the path is only partly backed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 pre-sales guidance of INR 6,500 crore was held unchanged, not raised, with H1 at about 40% and Q2 pre-sales down 5% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 must deliver about INR 3,900 crore (about 60% of INR 6,500 crore) against a flat H1, and it depends on three launches (Chembur Q4, Nagpur Q4, Pune before December) with pending IOD, final approval and RERA steps.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Three launches guided: Suman Nagar (Chembur) in Q4 FY27, Nagpur plotted project in Q4 after approvals, and Blossoms (Pune) before December; Elaara (Bangur Nagar) already launched mid-September with 30% sold.

rows.label: Kalpataru Park City Thane demand ramp
rows.why: Thane H1 FY27 pre-sales about INR 420 crore vs INR 167 crore in H1 FY26 (up about 130%); management expects over 3,000 families on site by FY28 from about 2,000 now.

rows.label: Net debt flat at FY27 year-end
rows.why: Net debt was INR 8,323 crore at 30 Sep 2026 (2.1x net debt-to-equity), and guidance is flat vs FY26, so deleveraging depends on H2 completions and collections.

rows.label: Price increases of 3% to 5% across projects
rows.why: Price increases of 3% to 5% have been taken across projects to cover current inflation and cost increases, with no further headroom quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand breadth, Thane and the completion target, and the guidance was held; analysts pressed on the H1-to-H2 bridge to INR 6,500 crore, launch approvals and price headroom, and several answers stayed qualitative, such as Kalpataru One.
